text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing is spread across every complexity stratum, including many low-complexity patients, but with no documented 99215 claims the pattern is a strong screening signal rather than a confirmed finding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running roughly double the all-provider rate in every condition band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition, so a sicker panel does not explain the excess on its own. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s for presentations such as upper respiratory infection, low back pain, rash and follow-up visits (e.g., C0059773, C0060059, C0060461, C0060821), which is a pattern consistent with upcoding, while the high-complexity sample (e.g., C0059990, C0061109) looks clinically plausible for top-level visits. The documentation is too thin to judge: only 15 charts came back, none for a 99215, and the single unsupported 99214 (C0061480) plus one moderate-data note without a lab line are each too few to carry weight. A reviewer should first request records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition minor-complaint visits, and check documented MDM and time against the billed level. A comparison set of the high-complexity 99215 charts would show whether documentation differs meaningfully by patient acuity."}
